sentences.en: In other words, the whole point is LLMs are now consumers of programming languages.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，关键在于大语言模型现在成了编程语言的消费者。

sentences.en: You know, I could take advantage of this kind of like pattern matching ability, or I could recognize that using my pattern matching
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可以利用这种类似模式匹配的能力，或者我可以认识到，利用我的模式匹配

sentences.en: ability, this is a really classic programming thing.
sentences.zh: 能力，这是一个非常经典的编程问题。

sentences.en: I shall write some code.
sentences.zh: 我应该写点代码。

sentences.en: And that I think is interesting.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有意思。

sentences.en: So LLMs are becoming consumers of our languages.
sentences.zh: 所以大语言模型正在成为我们语言的消费者。

sentences.en: And by default, it shows Python.

sentences.zh: 所以我们再次看到了这种强化。

sentences.en: There's all of these things that are effectively decelerating what's happening in the mainstream of languages, which is not to say that there isn't interesting stuff happening.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情实际上都在减缓主流语言领域的发展速度，这并不是说没有发生有趣的事情。

sentences.en: I just want to say that's out in the long tail.
sentences.zh: 我只想说那些还在长尾效应中。

sentences.en: Whether it breaks through to the mainstream, well, it's, it's, the road has got a lot steeper.
sentences.zh: 至于它能否突破进入主流，嗯，这条路变得陡峭多了。

sentences.en: That's, that's, that's kind of the issue.

sentences.en: of actually are and how they are rolling into, still rolling into languages.

sentences.en: And it's slowly been coming into languages.

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a nine, that's a mid 1970s idea.

sentences.zh: 关键是，60 和 70 年代的这些创新现在依然在进入各种语言中。

sentences.en: And there's not a lot of novelty in the mainstream space.
sentences.zh: 主流领域并没有太多的新意。

sentences.zh: 而且这种现象正在自我强化。

sentences.en: I think what we're going to see is in the next decade or two is that languages adopt these features.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在未来十年或二十年里将会看到的是，编程语言会采纳这些特性。

sentences.zh: 所以 10 年后的 Python 可能拥有全套更多的新特性。

sentences.zh: C++ 将会，好吧，C++ 每隔三年就会有天翻地覆的变化。

sentences.zh: 所以语言本身在原地发生着变化，但语言的集合变化得越来越慢。

sentences.zh: 不是这周吧？

十名了。

sentences.en: And I usually go one for three or two for three.
sentences.zh: 我通常能中一个或两个。

sentences.zh: 但自从两三年前我开始这样做以来，我的预测之一就是 Rust，我记得它的排名大概是第 13 或第 12 位，将会挤进前十。

sentences.en: And every year it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 结果每年都没有。

sentences.en: It just stays where it is.
sentences.zh: 它就原封不动地呆在那里。

sentences.en: I can't remember if I predicted it last year.
sentences.zh: 我不记得去年我是不是这么预测的了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so yeah, I'm always, you always think, oh, there's a lot of momentum, but you forget how many decades and millions, if not billions of lines

sentences.en: of C++ code there are out there.
sentences.zh: C++ 代码存在。

sentences.zh: 在接下来的五到十年里，我们不会看到什么大的转变？

sentences.zh: 还是会出现更多像 TypeScript 取代 JavaScript 这样的情况？

sentences.zh: 别忘了 TypeScript 是微软的。

sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这里面有一种很有趣的联系。

sentences.en: That Anders Halesberg interview, maybe I'll send Connor the link because that's an interesting one because he's obviously talking about TypeScript there.

sentences.en: But there is a case that in some of these cases, every single ranking is going to have some kind of spotlight bias on what it focuses on.

sentences.zh: 我在演讲中讨论过的那一点是，我总是说，嗯，在看 GitHub 时，人们必须，其实我并没有讨论那里的微软偏差，

sentences.zh: 特别是，新软件的体现会清晰得多。
